items.stem: Explain what is meant by an integrated accounting system.
items.answer: One in which the sales, purchases, inventory, payroll and general ledgers are linked, so a single entry updates all the relevant records and reports.

items.stem: Explain why control accounts are still useful in a computerised system.

items.stem: Explain the meaning of "garbage in, garbage out" in computerised accounting.
items.answer: The output is only as accurate as the data entered; if wrong figures or codes are input, the reports will be wrong even though the processing is accurate.

items.stem: The finance manager of Tamarind Ltd says, "Our accounting software always produces a balanced trial balance, so our accounts must be correct." The auditor found that a receipt of $39,800 from customer K. Osei was posted to the account of K. Owusu. Explain why the manager is wrong, referring to this error.

items.markingKey: Balanced TB only proves equal debits/credits [1]; names the type of error [1]; effect on accounts [1] [3]

items.answer: Computerised: volume of transactions, aged receivables, automatic statements.

items.stem: Pinnacle Ltd is considering accounting software costing $18,500 to install plus an annual licence of $1,700. It will save 21 hours of clerical time per week at $15 per hour for 48 weeks a year. Calculate the net annual benefit and the payback period.
items.answer: Net benefit $13,420 a year; payback 1.4 years

items.stem: Quetzal plc is considering accounting software costing $31,000 to install plus an annual licence of $4,700. It will save 15 hours of clerical time per week at $20 per hour for 50 weeks a year and reduce irrecoverable debts by $5,100 a year through better credit control. Calculate the net annual benefit and the payback period.
items.answer: Net benefit $15,400 a year; payback 2.0 years

items.stem: Banyan Ltd, a wholesaler in Manila, keeps manual ledgers. The owner is considering an integrated accounting package costing $21,500 plus training of $3,700 and an annual licence of $6,200. The change would allow 2 clerks earning $16,000 a year to be redeployed. (a) Calculate the annual net saving and the payback period. (b) Explain two risks of the change and how each could be controlled.
items.answer: (a) $25,800; 1.0 years (b) Data loss — regular off-site/cloud backups; unauthorised access/fraud — passwords and user access levels; input errors — validation checks and training.

items.answer: Allows payment fraud; restrict to authorised users and require independent verification.

items.stem: At Lynx Ltd, one accounts clerk sets up new suppliers, enters purchase invoices and releases payments using a shared password. Over 6 months the clerk paid $24,500 to a fictitious supplier before the fraud was found. The company has no off-site backup of its accounting data. (a) Identify two weaknesses in the internal controls. (b) Explain why off-site backups are needed.
items.answer: (a) No segregation of duties; shared password/no individual access levels; no review of new suppliers; no backups. (b) Fire, theft, hardware failure or ransomware could destroy the only copy of the records; backups allow recovery and continued trading.
